output.summary: The record year is mostly a commodity effect: corn rose 46% and the auditor ties the merchandising gain to price appreciation, while volume fell 0.9% and peers without any program grew revenue and savings faster than Cottonwood did. The 6% cost-per-bushel gain comes from maintenance spend falling from 2.8 to 1.9 cents while the deferred backlog tripled to $1.26M. Drying depends on one nearing-retirement superintendent with no successor. Harlan Junction has open insurer-required dust and monitoring findings due 21 Nov. Corrective action on those hazards is preferred now. The expansion vote is premature: its baseline uses inflated revenue and its throughput growth is unsourced. Holding maintenance flat is harmful.
